highlights_headline: SkiaSharp 4.151.0 adds the Graphite GPU backend for Vulkan, Metal, and Dawn, plus async pixel readback.
highlights_body: A new `SkiaSharp.Vulkan.Silk.NET` package ships alongside the Graphite bindings. Performance gets two targeted fixes: `SKData.SaveTo` avoids a double buffer copy and uniform lookups in `SKRuntimeEffectUniforms` are pre-sized. Skia m151 upstream stability fixes are also included.

bullets.detail: The bundled engine picks up two rounds of upstream chrome/m151 bug fixes and a submodule sync.

bullets.lead: Graphite GPU backend — Vulkan, Metal, and Dawn
bullets.detail: New managed bindings expose Skia's next-generation Graphite rendering backend with contexts for Vulkan, Metal, and Dawn, alongside a new `SkiaSharp.Vulkan.Silk.NET` package that wires Graphite Vulkan to the Silk.NET interop layer.

bullets.lead: Async pixel readback on SKImage and SKSurface
bullets.detail: `RequestReadPixels` is a backend-neutral async API that lets callers read pixels off the GPU without blocking the render thread.
A `CoTaskMem`-allocated pixel buffer was leaked when the raster image creation path failed; the allocation is now correctly freed on the failure path.
The `SaveTo` path now writes directly from the native buffer, eliminating an intermediate managed copy that doubled peak memory usage for large data objects.
`SKRuntimeEffectUniforms` now pre-sizes its internal uniform-name map to the known count, avoiding repeated rehashing on first use in hot render loops.

bullets.lead: GetEncodedText avoids string allocation in null-terminated path
bullets.detail: The fast path for null-terminated text no longer allocates an intermediate string, reducing GC pressure in text-heavy rendering.

bullets.lead: FreeType font support on Nano Server
bullets.detail: Nano Server containers gain font rendering through FreeType, enabling server-side text layout in minimal Windows container environments.

bullets.lead: Azure Linux, Alpine/musl, and Nano Server test coverage
bullets.detail: Containerized test legs for Azure Linux, Alpine (musl libc), and Nano Server are now part of the CI matrix, widening platform validation.
